identifier: Configure your backup region
statement: Your backup region is automatically set to your store's home country when you create your store.

identifier: Review your default markets
statement: When you create a Shopify store, the following markets are created for you automatically: * Domestic market: Your store's home country or region, as determined by your store's address and currency. This is your domestic market and represents the default customer experience. The country in your domestic market is set as your backup region by default. * International market: A curated list of countries or regions where merchants similar to you also sell. This market is inactive by default.

identifier: Change your primary market
statement: Your primary market is the main country or region that you sell to. It's typically your domestic market, and represents the default customer experience for your store. Review the following characteristics of the primary market: * Your primary market can contain only one country or region. * Your primary market can't be deleted. * All changes to your store's default settings apply to your primary market automatically. * Your primary market is determined by your store currency in Settings > General. For example, if your store address is in the United States but your currency is set to Canadian dollars, then your primary market is set to Canada.

identifier: Change your primary market
statement: Markets with subfolders configured can't be made into a primary market, because it would create broken URLs. Update the domain settings first. Markets with more than one region also can't be made primary, because primary markets are limited to one region.

identifier: Market nodes, Business entity
statement: A market node's business entity section displays the name of the business entity associated with that market.

identifier: Setting up business entities for markets
statement: By default, all orders in your store are processed through your primary Shopify Payments account, which is associated with your store's home country. If you have multiple Shopify Payments accounts for different legal entities in different countries, then you can assign each entity to the appropriate market.

identifier: Conversion fees
statement: The currency conversion fee is charged when a customer pays in a currency that's different from your Shopify Payments payout currency. The fee is either 1.5% or 2%, depending on your store's location.

identifier: Currency conversion fee rates based on store location for Shopify Payments merchants.
statement: Store location Conversion fee United States 1.5% United Kingdom, European Economic Area, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and other regions 2%

identifier: Fees and multi-entity stores
statement: If your store uses multiple business entities with Shopify Payments accounts in different countries, then the conversion fee depends on which entity processes the payment. If the customer's payment currency matches the entity's payout currency, then no conversion fee is charged.

identifier: Supported currencies
statement: Shopify Payments supports several currencies for international selling. The currencies available to you depend on your store's location and your payment processor. If a country's local currency isn't supported by Shopify Payments, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed to customers in that country instead.

identifier: Backup region and the domestic market
statement: When you first create your store, your domestic market is created automatically with your home country, and the backup region is set to that same country. This means unmatched customers receive the same experience as your domestic customers, without the ability to complete a checkout.

identifier: Determining tax on the Managed Markets fee {#fee-tax}
statement: In some countries, the Managed Markets fee is taxable. Whether the fee is taxed depends on the address associated with the legal business name on your store. This address determines both whether tax is added to the fee, and which tax applies: * If your legal business address is in the United States, then no tax is added to the Managed Markets fee. * If your legal business address is in the United Kingdom, then VAT is added to the Managed Markets fee. * If your legal business address is in Canada, then GST, HST, QST, PST, or RST is added to the Managed Markets fee, depending on your province.

identifier: Delivered duty paid (DDP) shipping
statement: Stores in the United States can buy DHL Express, DHL eCommerce, and FedEx labels. Stores in Canada and the United Kingdom can buy DHL Express and FedEx labels.

identifier: Fraud and chargebacks {#fraud}
statement: If your store is based in the United States, then your Managed Markets orders are automatically reviewed for fraud, and eligible orders are protected from fraud chargebacks with Shopify Protect.

identifier: Change your store address {#change-your-store-address}
statement: Changing your store's country might affect the following details: * Your subscription fees and billing currency. * The local language and currency for your store. * Your tax and duty obligations. * Shipping availability. * Your access to Shopify products and services.

identifier: billing address
statement: The company name and address on your Shopify bills come from your billing address, which is a separate setting from your store address. Changing your store address doesn't change your billing address.

identifier: Change your store address {#change-your-store-address}
statement: If your store uses financial services such as Shopify Payments, Shopify Balance, Shopify Capital, or Shopify Credit, then you need to deactivate all financial services before you can change your store's country in your Shopify admin.

identifier: Managing your Shopify billing address
statement: Your billing address is the registered address that you pay Shopify from, and it's the address displayed on your Shopify bills. Your billing address determines the billing taxes that apply to your account, the payment methods and billing currencies that are available to you, and the Shopify company that issues your bill.

identifier: Settings > Billing > Billing profile, Address and currency
statement: You can manage your billing address in the Address and currency section of the Settings > Billing > Billing profile page of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Requirements for your billing address
statement: Your billing address is subject to the following validation rules that don't apply to your store address: * The country of your billing address must match the country of one of your active business entities. You select the entity when you change your address, so you can't enter a country that you don't have an entity in. Learn more about managing business entities. * Your billing currency must be supported for the country of your billing address. If the country that you select doesn't support your current billing currency, then you need to select a supported currency before you can save the address.

identifier: Change your billing address
statement: If your store is on the Shopify Plus plan, then your address and currency are specified by your Shopify Plus contract and you can't change them yourself. To update them, contact Shopify Plus Support.

Private Partnership A business jointly owned and operated by two or more partners, typically with shared management responsibilities, profits, losses, and liability. identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets
statement: Your store currency must be the default currency of the country where your business is based. For example, a business that's based in the United States needs a store currency of USD. If your store currency is different, then you can't activate Managed Markets.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets
statement: In addition to meeting these requirements, there are requirements for Managed Markets specific to where your business is based.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in the United States
statement: To use Managed Markets in the United States, you need to meet the following requirements: * Your business needs to be based in the continental United States (exclusive of territories including Puerto Rico and Guam). * Your business needs at least one non-PO box location in the United States. * You need at least one fulfillment location in the continental United States.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in Canada
statement: To use Managed Markets in Canada, you need to meet the following requirements: * Your business needs to be based in Canada. * Your business needs at least one non-PO box location in Canada. * You need at least one fulfillment location in Canada. * If you have multiple fulfillment locations in Canada, then all your fulfillment locations must be located within the same province. * Your store must use Shopify Tax or Basic Tax. Managed Markets can't be used if your store uses manual tax settings.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: To use Managed Markets in the United Kingdom, you need to meet the following requirements: * Your business needs to be based in the United Kingdom. * Your business needs at least one non-PO box location in the United Kingdom. * You need at least one fulfillment location in the United Kingdom. * If you have multiple fulfillment locations in the United Kingdom, then all your fulfillment locations must be located either within Great Britain or Northern Ireland. If you have fulfillment locations in both Great Britain and Northern Ireland, then you can't use Managed Markets.

identifier: Managed Markets comparison table: Cross-border payments
statement: Receive payouts in USD for stores based in the United States, CAD for stores based in Canada, and GBP for stores based in the United Kingdom.

identifier: Managed Markets comparison table: Cross-border payments
statement: Use Shopify Payments for domestic transactions and Managed Markets for international transactions.

identifier: Managed Markets changes to your store: Checkout
statement: Shipping with prepaid duties is used at checkout. In the United States, shipping is available with DHL Express, DHL eCommerce, UPS, and FedEx. In the United Kingdom and Canada, shipping is available with DHL Express and FedEx.

identifier: Activate Managed Markets: self-billing agreement
statement: If your store is based in the United Kingdom or Canada, then you need to sign a self-billing agreement when you activate Managed Markets. A self-billing agreement is required for tax compliance.

identifier: Managed Markets for Canada
statement: Managed Markets is available for stores based in Canada.

identifier: Considerations for using Managed Markets in Canada
statement: The following features aren't yet available for Managed Markets in Canada: * Shopify Protect. * Multi-currency payouts. * Refunds for Managed Markets orders.

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in Canada
statement: You can purchase DHL Express and FedEx shipping labels for Managed Markets orders in Canada. Canada Post, DHL eCommerce, and UPS aren't available.

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in Canada
statement: Shipping labels purchased through Managed Markets in Canada are zero-rated. You aren't charged tax on the cost of your Managed Markets shipping labels.

identifier: Payouts and fees for Managed Markets in Canada: Fees
statement: GST, HST, QST, PST, or RST is added to the Managed Markets fee for stores based in Canada, depending on your province.

identifier: Merchant of record fee invoices
statement: When you activate Managed Markets, Global-e becomes your merchant of record for international Managed Markets orders. In Canada, you're charged a merchant of record service fee directly.

identifier: Managed Markets tax invoices for Canada
statement: A Managed Markets order in Canada is considered a business-to-business (B2B) sale from your store to Global-e, who then sells to your customer as the merchant of record. As a result, Managed Markets sales in Canada have tax implications. In Canada, GST, HST, QST, PST, or RST applies to orders, depending on your province.

identifier: Tax ID validation
statement: In Canada, your GST or HST tax ID is validated, along with your business name. Your GST or HST registration must match your registered legal business name. If your tax registration is invalid or doesn't match your legal business name, then you might be liable for the tax due on your Managed Markets sales.

identifier: Managed Markets for the United Kingdom
statement: Managed Markets is available for stores based in the United Kingdom.

identifier: Considerations for using Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: The following features aren't yet available for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom: * Shopify Protect. * Multi-currency payouts. * Refunds for Managed Markets orders.

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: You can purchase DHL Express and FedEx shipping labels for Managed Markets orders in the United Kingdom. DHL eCommerce and UPS aren't available.

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: Shipping labels purchased through Managed Markets in the United Kingdom are zero-rated. You aren't charged tax on the cost of your Managed Markets shipping labels.

identifier: Payouts and fees for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom: Fees
statement: VAT is added to the Managed Markets fee for stores based in the United Kingdom.

identifier: Merchant of record fee invoices
statement: When you activate Managed Markets, Global-e becomes your merchant of record for international Managed Markets orders. In the United Kingdom, you're charged a merchant of record service fee directly.

identifier: Managed Markets tax invoices for the United Kingdom
statement: A Managed Markets order in the United Kingdom is considered a business-to-business (B2B) sale from your store to Global-e, who then sells to your customer as the merchant of record. As a result, Managed Markets sales in the United Kingdom have tax implications. In the United Kingdom, VAT applies to orders.

identifier: Tax ID validation
statement: In the United Kingdom, your VAT tax ID and business name are validated. Your VAT registration must be valid and match your registered legal business name. If your VAT registration is invalid or doesn't match your legal business name, then you might be liable for 20% VAT due on your Managed Markets sales.

identifier: Payouts and fees for Managed Markets: Fees
statement: Managed Markets has the following fees for international orders: * A Shopify Payments processing fee, which varies by your Shopify plan and the payment method used by your customer. * A Managed Markets transaction fee of 3.25% for stores on the Shopify Plus plan, or 3.5% for stores on the Basic, Grow, or Advanced plan. * A currency conversion fee that's the same as the foreign exchange (FX) fee for Shopify Payments in your region.

identifier: Create a new store {#create-new-store} (Overview of expansion stores for organizations on the Shopify Plus plan)
statement: You can create an expansion store in the Organization section of your Shopify admin. Note Before creating a new store in your organization, your main store must have a payment method added under Settings > Billing and a complete billing address under Settings > General > Store Details > Store address. Steps: 1. From your Shopify admin, go to Settings > Organization. 2. Click Create store. 3. In the Store type section, select whether the store is for Staging or Production. 5. In the Profile section, enter a name and a store URL. 6. Optional: In the Internal name and icon section, enter a name and a two-letter or three-letter initial for the store. The name and initials that you enter in this section display within the Shopify admin only, and don't display to customers. 7. Optional: To import data, in the Import data from an existing store section, click Select store, and then select the store. 8. Optional: Select the data that you want to copy to your new store by completing any of the following steps: * To select a theme, do either of the following: * If there is more than one theme in the store that you selected, then click Select themes to select the themes that you want to copy. * If there is only one theme in the store that you selected, then select Themes to copy the theme. * Select Products and Collections to copy all the products, variants, and their metafields (excluding reference types). * Select Files to copy all files, including all images and videos. 9. Click Create Store.
scope: organizations on the Shopify Plus plan

identifier: Plan fees and charges {#fees-and-charges}: billing currency by location
statement: The Basic, Grow, and Advanced pricing plans have multiple rates and fees, such as monthly price, credit card rates, and third-party transaction fees. Depending on your location, your subscription is billed in one of the following currencies: * Euros (EUR) * British pounds (GBP) * US dollars (USD) * Indian rupees (INR)

identifier: Credit card rates {#credit-card-rates}: Brexit
statement: As a result of Brexit, Visa and Mastercard have changed how they classify and charge for United Kingdom (UK) and European Union (EU) transactions. To comply with these changes, Shopify classifies these transactions as international, and you're charged at the current international rate for your region.

identifier: Third-party payment providers {#third-party-payment}
statement: If Shopify Payments isn't available in your country, or if you prefer not to use it, then you can activate one of the third-party payment providers that integrates with Shopify. In this case, Shopify charges third-party transaction fees which vary depending on the plan that you choose. Your third-party payment provider charges you their credit card rates themselves, separately.

identifier: Local pricing for your Shopify subscription plan
statement: In some regions, Shopify offers subscription plan prices that are adjusted to the local cost of living. Eligibility for local pricing for Shopify plans is determined based on where your store is located. The Shopify Terms of Service require you to maintain an accurate location based on your current jurisdiction. In regions where local pricing for Shopify subscription plans is available, the subscription rate for your plan is applied when you sign up. If you open a new store, then your local prices are automatically displayed. If your store was opened prior to the availability of local pricing and is located in a region with local pricing, then you can switch your subscription plan to the local rate by changing to the same plan priced according to the local rate. Local pricing applies only to Shopify subscription plan rates.

identifier: Setting up international sales tools {#shopify-markets} (Shopify Plus plan launch checklist)
statement: You can set up international sales tools to sell cross-border and expand your business to other countries and regions. Managed Markets is available only to businesses based in the United States.
scope: the page: Shopify Plus plan launch checklist

identifier: Regional availability of selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: To sell from multiple entities with Shopify Payments, your entities must be located in a country where Shopify Payments is supported.

identifier: Entity selection for transactions: POS
statement: For POS transactions, the physical location where the POS device is logged in determines the entity. Each POS location maps to a specific business entity during setup, and staff can't manually change the entity during checkout. The entity must be in the same country as the POS location.

identifier: Set up separate entities for each country with retail locations
statement: To manage retail businesses across multiple regions, you must have a separate entity for each country with retail locations, including pop-up locations.

identifier: Customer data hosting locations (Understanding customer privacy settings in your Shopify admin)
statement: In the Customer data hosting location section, you can find the primary location where Shopify stores your store data, order data, and customer personal data. To learn more about data hosting locations, you can refer to the documentation on data hosting locations.

identifier: Understanding customer privacy settings in your Shopify Admin: region picker cards
statement: When you log in to your Shopify admin, you can set up a privacy policy, add a cookie banner, allow visitors to opt-out of their data being sold or shared, update your Shopify Network Intelligence settings, and view information about the geographic storage location of your data. Your setting for Shopify Network Intelligence takes effect globally, but your settings for cookie banners and data sharing can be managed per region. The region picker cards, which include a dialog listing all available countries and states, are used for configuring where the consent banner and opt-out page are displayed in your online store. These cards display the regions currently selected based on your configured markets.

identifier: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
statement: The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) imposes obligations and responsibilities with respect to personal data for businesses located in or offering goods or services to individuals in the European Economic Area, and Switzerland and the United Kingdom have adopted equivalent laws for UK and Swiss businesses and residents. By using Shopify, there are tools and information that you can use to help you to analyze your business practices and help ensure that you comply with your GDPR obligations. Using services offered by Shopify alone doesn't guarantee that you comply with GDPR. You're generally the controller of your customers’ data. This means that you choose how your customers’ data is handled. If you make goods and services available to individuals in Europe, even if you or your business aren't located in Europe, then GDPR might apply to your business.

identifier: Using Shopify to help comply with GDPR: where personal data is processed or stored
statement: The GDPR doesn't require personal data to be processed or stored in Europe. The GDPR requires personal data of European residents transferred outside of Europe to be protected in accordance with applicable laws. Learn more about international data transfers.

identifier: Pixels overview, Customer privacy {#customer-privacy}: Note
statement: You're responsible for your own privacy compliance, and you should consult your own legal counsel to determine how the laws in your region, and the region in which you sell, might affect your business. To sell products using the Shopify platform, you must comply with the laws of the jurisdiction of your business and your customers, the Shopify Terms of Service, the Shopify Acceptable Use Policy, and any other applicable policies.

identifier: Launch your store {#remove-your-online-store-password}: required steps
statement: Before you can launch your store, you must complete the following required steps: * Select a subscription plan. If you pick a plan during a free trial, then you won't be charged any subscription fees until your free trial expires. * Add a store address to the Business details section of the Settings > General page. * Set up a payment method, and make sure that test mode is deactivated.

identifier: Contact information requirements by the European Economic Area
statement: If you're a merchant located in, or shipping to, the European Economic Area, or if you're a merchant targeting consumers in the European Economic Area, then you're required to include your company number and Value-Added Tax (VAT) number on your online store.

identifier: Required legal notice for using Shopify Payments in Japan {#required-pages-for-using-shopify-payments-in-japan}
statement: If you use Shopify Payments in Japan, then you're required to have a legal notice containing information for the Specified Commercial Transactions Act (特定商取引法に基づく表記). Add this legal notice in the Legal notice section of Settings > Policies, and not as a page.

identifier: Country and currency compliance for Shopify POS
statement: When you process a POS transaction in person using Shopify Payments and a Shopify card reader, you must follow the payment rules for the country you're processing the transaction in.

identifier: Country and currency compliance for Shopify POS: multiple countries
statement: To accept in-person POS payments in multiple countries, you must create a separate Shopify store and Shopify Payments account for each additional country.

identifier: Requirements for country compliance {#requirements}
statement: To remain compliant with country requirements when making in-person sales, your business must meet the following criteria: * Your Shopify store's country must match the country of all your physical stores' locations. * Your Shopify store currency must match the local currency of your physical stores' locations. * Your store's currency must match your Shopify Payments payout bank account currency. These requirements apply only to physical locations where you accept payments with Shopify Payments.

identifier: Requirements for country compliance {#requirements}: where they don't apply
statement: In-person country requirements don't apply in the following circumstances: * In-person sales in an international location using a payment solution other than Shopify Payments. * International locations that don't accept payments. For example, locations for warehousing or inventory management.

identifier: Setting up SMS notifications
statement: You can give your customers the option of entering a phone number at checkout instead of an email address. If you have SMS notifications set up, and if your business address is in a supported country, then customers who enter a phone number instead of an email address will receive their order confirmation by SMS to their mobile phone.

identifier: Supported countries for SMS notifications {#supported-countries}
statement: SMS notifications are supported only when your business address is in one of the following countries: * Australia * Brazil * Canada * France * Germany * Ireland * Italy * Japan * New Zealand * Spain * United Kingdom * United States If your business isn't in a supported country, then you can only offer email notifications to customers, or you must install a transactional SMS app from the Shopify App Store.

identifier: Improved clarity for managing Business details (Shopify Changelog, January 22, 2026)
statement: You can now manage your store’s business details in the General settings page with an updated Business details section. This makes it easier to keep the information Shopify needs for verification and financial services up to date—without having to wait for onboarding or remediation.

identifier: Improved clarity for managing Business details: Store address (Store contact details)
statement: We’ve renamed the Billing address section in Store contact details to Store address to better reflect what that address represents. This does not change how your address is used.

identifier: Improved clarity for managing Business details: the store's currency and the business country
statement: Your store’s currency is now set based on the business country selected in Business details.

identifier: Improved clarity for managing Business details: Note (financial products active)
statement: Note: If you have financial products such as Shopify Payments or Shopify Capital active you will need to deactivate these before making changes.
scope: stores with financial products such as Shopify Payments or Shopify Capital active

identifier: Store address compared to billing address (Settings > General > Store contact details)
statement: Your store address is the physical or customer-facing address of your business. Customers can view this address on your store and policy pages. You can manage it in the **Store contact details** section of the **Settings** > [**General**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/general) page.

identifier: Store address compared to billing address: two separate settings
statement: You maintain the two addresses independently. Changing your store address doesn't change your billing address, and changing your billing address doesn't change your store address.

identifier: Best practices for writing marketing emails with Shopify Messaging: Note on the store address
statement: Your store address is the address on your invoices from Shopify. It can also affect which apps can be used in your store. Make sure that you're comfortable with using a PO box for these purposes before you update your store address.

identifier: Checklist for preparing your store for a transfer: business contact information
statement: Update the business contact information for your store in the [**General**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/general) settings page of your Shopify admin, including the store email, store phone, and business address.
scope: preparing a store for a transfer of ownership

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Currency, markets, and business entities {#currency-markets-and-business-entities}, Multiple business entities
statement: Multiple business entities: The entity assigned to each retail location determines the currency for Shopify POS at that location, including how the location maps to its Retail market.
scope: Shopify POS; stores with multiple business entities

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Currency, markets, and business entities {#currency-markets-and-business-entities}, in-person card payments in a country's local currency
statement: To process in-person card payments using integrated card readers in a country’s local currency, the entity for that location must use a default payout currency that matches the country and currency requirements for that country.

identifier: Country-specific retail requirements: cross-entity returns and exchanges
statement: In France, Spain, Italy, Germany, and Sweden, a return or exchange against an original sale must be processed by the same legal entity as the original sale to be compliant.
scope: Shopify POS in France, Spain, Italy, Germany and Sweden

identifier: Retail requirements in Spain {#spain}: product bundles
statement: You can't sell product bundles in Shopify POS for retail locations in Spain.

identifier: General tax set-up steps, step 1 (default location)
statement: Determine where you have an obligation to collect tax. This typically starts with your default location and where you operate your business from. This is usually your home country, province, or state.

identifier: Requirements for buying shipping labels {#ss-availability}
statement: To buy shipping labels in Shopify, your business needs to have an eligible fulfillment location and for some carriers your store needs to be based in the same country as the fulfillment location.

identifier: Requirements for buying shipping labels {#ss-availability}: Evri and DPD
statement: For example, if you want to buy shipping labels from Evri or DPD, then you need to have a fulfillment location in the United Kingdom and your store's address needs to be based in the United Kingdom.
scope: Evri and DPD shipping labels (United Kingdom)

identifier: Cash rounding rules {#cash-rounding-rules}
statement: Cash rounding rules might apply automatically at checkout depending on your store's location and when you opened your store in a particular country. Some rules apply to all stores in specific countries.

identifier: Cash rounding rules {#cash-rounding-rules}: new stores and first retail locations
statement: Starting July 26, 2026, additional rules apply to new stores created on or after July 6, 2026, and to existing stores that set up their first retail location in a listed country on or after July 6, 2026.

identifier: Retail requirements in Italy: automatic receipt printing
statement: Automatic receipt printing is on by default for Shopify POS locations in Italy. If you turn off automatic receipt printing, then you're responsible for making sure that each sale has a proper fiscal document.

identifier: Pricing and billing for SMS marketing campaigns: toll-free numbers
statement: A $2.15 USD monthly charge applies to each approved toll-free number used for SMS marketing in the United States and Canada.
scope: Shopify Messaging, SMS marketing campaigns; the United States and Canada

identifier: Requirements and guidelines for sending SMS marketing campaigns: Region-specific requirements (European Union)
statement: If you're located in or sending marketing messages to countries in the European Union, then your store must be compliant with the ePrivacy Directive.
scope: Shopify Messaging, SMS marketing campaigns; stores located in or sending marketing messages to countries in the European Union

identifier: Requirements and guidelines for sending SMS marketing campaigns: Region-specific requirements (United Kingdom)
statement: If you're located in or sending marketing messages to the United Kingdom, then your store must be compliant with the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations.
scope: Shopify Messaging, SMS marketing campaigns; stores located in or sending marketing messages to the United Kingdom

identifier: Supported recipient countries for SMS marketing campaigns {#supported-countries}
statement: There are no specific country requirements for your store's location, as long as it meets the requirements for sending SMS marketing campaigns. However, you can send SMS marketing messages only to customers located in the following countries:

identifier: Pricing and billing for SMS marketing campaigns
statement: In addition to the per-message cost, other charges apply depending on your region and the types of messages you send. If you send SMS marketing messages to the United States or Canada, then a monthly fee applies for your toll-free number.

identifier: Per-SMS message charges
statement: You're charged based on the number of SMS marketing messages sent to each recipient. For example, if you're located in Denmark and you send 1,000 messages to recipients in Denmark, then you're billed $80 USD.

identifier: Eligibility requirements {#requirements}: business entity
statement: Your business entity must not be registered in China.

identifier: Eligibility requirements {#requirements}: stores located in Brazil or Indonesia
statement: If your store is located in Brazil or Indonesia, then you can send WhatsApp messages to customers in your own country, but you must verify and scale your account with Meta in any of the following ways to send marketing messages to other countries:
scope: Shopify Messaging, WhatsApp marketing campaigns; stores located in Brazil or Indonesia

identifier: Eligibility requirements {#requirements}: stores located in Brazil or Indonesia
statement: * Verify your business with Meta. * Scale your message sending by reaching a minimum of 1,000 business-initiated conversations per day, per phone number for 30 consecutive days.
scope: Shopify Messaging, WhatsApp marketing campaigns; stores located in Brazil or Indonesia

identifier: Supported regions {#supported-regions}: United States
statement: WhatsApp marketing messages can’t be sent to customers in the United States. However, if your store is located in the United States, then you can still use WhatsApp to send marketing messages to your subscribers in other supported countries.
scope: Shopify Messaging, WhatsApp marketing campaigns; the United States

identifier: Supported regions {#supported-regions}: China
statement: Consumer-level WhatsApp use is banned in China. You can’t send WhatsApp marketing messages to customers in China, and WhatsApp isn’t supported for Shopify stores based in China.
scope: Shopify Messaging, WhatsApp marketing campaigns; China

identifier: Supported regions {#supported-regions}: Sanctioned regions
statement: WhatsApp marketing isn't supported in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Donetsk, or Luhansk. You can't send WhatsApp marketing messages to customers or use WhatsApp marketing for your Shopify store in these locations.
scope: Shopify Messaging, WhatsApp marketing campaigns; Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk

identifier: Pricing and billing for WhatsApp marketing campaigns
statement: When you send WhatsApp messages using Shopify Messaging, you're charged per message and you're billed monthly. Marketing messages and service messages are billed at different rates for your region.

statement: هل يستطيع الأجنبي ممارسة التجارة الإلكترونية في السعودية؟ وقد يسأل آخرون: هل موقع سلة للسعوديين فقط؟ هل يحق للأجنبي فتح متجر الكتروني في السعودية؟ هل يحق للمقيم فتح متجر إلكتروني؟ إن خدمات التجارة الإلكترونية متاحة للسعوديين وذلك بعد استيفائهم للشروط النظامية، ومنها على سبيل المثال: إصدار وثيقة عمل حر - سجل تجاري. وللأجانب بعد استيفائهم للشروط النظامية، ومنها على سبيل المثال: إصدار ترخيص ممارسة التجارة الإلكترونية عبر وزارة الاستثمار.

identifier: ما هي اللغة الافتراضية للمتجر؟
statement: اللغة الافتراضية للمتجر: هي اللغة التي ستُعتمد في التعريف الأساسي لأقسام المتجر (واجهات - قوائم - منتجات - تصنيفات - الفروع - العروض - الإعلانات - ..).

identifier: هل يمكنني تغيير اللغة الافتراضية متى شئت؟

identifier: شروط وأحكام زد باي > الشروط العامة
statement: يمكن فقط للشركات، والمؤسسات، والأشخاص، والمنظمات المسموح لهم إجراء عمليات دفع واستلام أموال داخل بلادهم من الجهات الرسمية، الاشتراك لاستخدام زد باي. ولا يجوز استخدام زد باي ممن لا يسمح لهم باستلام الأموال أو القيام بعمليات تجارية أو غير تجارية داخل بلادهم.

identifier: شروط وأحكام زد باي > الأنشطة المحظورة
statement: لا يجوز للتاجر استخدام زد باي في أي نشاط محظور أو التعامل مع هيئات محظورة من زد باي أو المملكة العربية السعودية أو بلد النشاط، تتضمن: الأشخاص المتوفر عنهم معلومات باحتمالية تورطهم في نشاطات إجرامية أو مذكورين في اللوائح العامة (القائمة السوداء) للأنشطة الإجرامية والاتجار بالمخدرات والمنظمات الإرهابية. الأشخاص ذوو طبيعة نشاط من الصعب التحقق من شرعيته أو مصدر دخله، أو ذوو مصدر دخل لا يتوافق مع أوضاعهم المالية. الأشخاص الذين يرفضون تزويدنا بأي معلومات أو مستندات مطلوبة للتحقق من أنشطتهم أو مصادر الدخل أو الذين يزودونا بمستندات مشكوك في صحتها أو شرعيتها أو متلاعب بها. المؤسسات والشركات التي لا يمكن تحديد المساهمين فيها أو هيكلها التنظيمي. مكاتب الصرافة أو غيرها من الكيانات المشابهة غير المصرح لها. المؤسسات المالية المتمركزة في البلاد أو الأقاليم دون أن يكون لها حضورًا ماديًا والمشار إليها بـ (المصارف الصورية) والتي لا تنتمي إلى أي منظمة مالية خاضعة للرقابة. الأنشطة غير المتوافقة مع الشريعة الإسلامية. الوكلاء الوسطاء غير الرسميين. شركات العملات الرقمية مثل البيتكوين/ حسابات تداول العملات الرقمية. الأنشطة التي تتعامل بشكل مباشر أو غير مباشر مع البلدان الخاضعة للعقوبات الدولية، تتضمن (إيران، سوريا، جنوب السودان، كوبا، ارتريا، جمهورية افريقيا الوسطى) وما إلى ذلك. التجار الذين لا يقدموا أي معلومات كافية للتحقق من هوياتهم، أو هوية المستفيد النهائي. التاجر أو المستفيد النهائي (الشريك في عملية البيع والشراء) الذين طبقت عليهم عقوبات بناء على قرارات الأمم المتحدة، أو وزارة الخزانة الإنجليزية، أو الاتحاد الأوروبي، أو مكتب مراقبة الأصول الأجنبية، أو من هو مطالب للامتثال إذا كان الاسم مطابق لأي قائمة عقوبات أخرى. التاجر أو المستفيد النهائي ( الشريك في عملية البيع والشراء) الذي يقطن في البلدان الخاضعة للعقوبات الدولية تتضمن (إيران، سوريا، جنوب السودان، كوبا، ارتريا، جمهورية أفريقيا الوسطى) وما إلى ذلك. التجار مقدمي الخدمات المالية بدون موافقة البنك المركزي على سبيل المثال (الاستثمارات المالية غير المصرح بها، شركات التداول، تجميع الأموال أو الحوالات وخلافه). الجمعيات الخيرية والمنظمات غير الربحية غير المعتمدة من الجهات المعنية في المملكة العربية السعودية. الحسابات المجهولة والمسجلة بأسماء وهمية. الحسابات المرقمة التي يتعرف على مالكها بواسطة رقم بدلاً عن الأسماء. التجار الذين لم تكتمل إجراءات التحقق الواجبة عنهم أو لا يمكن التحري عنهم نظرًا لعدم اليقين أو الغموض في المعلومات المتوفرة عنهم. تجارة السجائر والسجائر الإلكترونية وجميع منتجات ومستلزمات التبغ. المراهنة/ المزاد. الأنشطة المحظورة أو المقيدة يمكن تحديثها في أي وقت، مع إشعار التاجر. المنتجات الرقمية : يتم قبول بعض المنتجات الرقمية بناء على تقييم نوع المنتجات من قبل مزود الخدمة أو أي نشاط آخر لا يتوافق مع مزود الخدمة.

identifier: WooCommerce > Settings > General
statement: To edit these settings, go to WooCommerce > Settings > General in your WordPress dashboard.

identifier: Store address
statement: This is where you set your business’s physical address — the location where you are based as a seller. Many tax and shipping configurations use this address for determining rates.

identifier: Supported countries (NOTE)
statement: For example, if you live in South Africa but your business is registered in the Sweden, you can use WooPayments for that business by selecting Sweden when signing up.

identifier: Signing up for WooPayments > Before you begin
statement: Be sure to select the correct country for your account, as it cannot be changed later. If you’re using WooPayments for a business, the relevant country is the one where your business is registered, not the one in which you personally live.

identifier: WooPayments is not listed in the Payments settings
statement: If WooPayments does not appear as an option in the Payments settings, then it’s likely that: The Business location at the top of the page is not set to one of our supported countries.

identifier: Requirements for WooPayments
statement: First, let’s make sure you have what’s required to ensure a smooth installation: Your business is based in one of our supported countries.

identifier: What information will I need? > Business information
statement: Business information Country where your business is based Type of business Industry Company address Company phone number Company URL EIN or other tax ID

identifier: How quickly will you confirm my identity?
statement: We’ll do our best to work with Stripe to confirm your identity as quickly as we can.

identifier: What else should I keep in mind?
statement: It’s not always possible to change account information once it’s been saved, especially if the site accepts live transactions before the correct account information is entered.

identifier: How can I change my information?
statement: Most of the KYC information can be changed via the Stripe dashboard.

identifier: Updating account information
statement: Updating certain account information can only be done in the Stripe Express dashboard.

identifier: Supported countries
statement: Australia Canada Finland Ireland Luxembourg Netherlands New Zealand Singapore United Kingdom United States

identifier: Supported countries > Phone POS availability
statement: Phone POS availability: Phone POS is currently available to UK merchants on iOS only (iOS 26+, WooMobile app 25.1+). Tablet POS remains available in all listed supported countries on both iOS and Android. Phone support for Android and additional countries is coming soon.

identifier: Can I take my card reader to another country for a convention or pop-up?
statement: No, live Terminal payments must be processed in the same country as the merchant’s account and associated reader location.

identifier: Can customers with foreign-issued cards pay on my card reader?
statement: Yes, as long as the merchant is using the reader in the supported country for their account and charging in the supported local currency.

identifier: All other supported countries
statement: For merchants in Canada, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Singapore, and the United Kingdom, we have the WisePad 3.

identifier: Recommended tax solutions
statement: Recommendations vary by your store country and by extensions that are already installed or active.

identifier: Calculate tax based on > Shop base address
statement: If you select Shop base address, taxes are always calculated based on your store’s location, regardless of the customer’s address.

identifier: Definitions > International Payment
statement: International Payment: An added percentage fee applied if the customer’s payment method originates from outside your WooPayments account country.

identifier: Notes for all countries
statement: VAT, GST, or Consumption Tax may apply to the WooPayments fees and are noted for each applicable country below. If your business is registered for VAT or GST, then you may qualify for a zero rate.

identifier: Countries in Europe
statement: For some countries, the International Payment fee is based on whether the customer used a European card or a non-European card. As a reference, WooPayments considers “European cards” to be those issued in any of the following countries: Andorra Austria Belgium Bulgaria Croatia Cyprus Czech Republic Denmark Estonia Faroe Islands Finland France Germany Gibraltar Greece Greenland Guernsey Hungary Iceland Ireland Isle of Man Israel Italy Jersey Latvia Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Malta Monaco Netherlands Norway Poland Portugal Romania St. Pierre and Miquelon San Marino Slovakia Slovenia Spain Sweden Türkiye Vatican City

identifier: Store Profile Settings: How It Works (Settings › Store profile; Storefront settings › Contact information)
statement: When you create a new store, the basic contact information you provide, such as the store name and email address, is added to the store profile. You can manage store information globally from Settings › Store profile, or you can add unique information to individual storefronts from Channels › Channel Manager by clicking the storefront’s name and going to Storefront settings › Contact information.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: How It Works: locale information
statement: If your store has 100,00 or more products or you have not enabled multi-language, you can also manage locale information for your store, such as the country where your store is located and the default language used for storefront content. These settings allow you to access region-specific payment methods and also automatically translate storefront content in supported languages.
scope: stores with 100,00 or more products, or that have not enabled multi-language

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Requirements: Manage Settings permission
statement: To view and manage store profile settings, the Manage Settings permission must be enabled on your user account.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Locale
statement: The Locale settings determine your store's country and customer-facing language.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Locale: Default country
statement: Default country — The country your store is run from, which determines the payment methods that are available for use with your store.

identifier: Store Settings: Requirements
statement: To view and manage your store’s settings, the Manage Settings permission must be enabled on your user account. Depending on the area being managed, you may need additional permissions. See the relevant linked articles for specific requirements.

identifier: Store Settings: Store Profile (Settings › Store profile)
statement: Provide basic information about your business, such as the store name, contact information, default country, and the default storefront language under Settings › Store profile.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions (Settings › Users)
statement: On BigCommerce, there are pre-made sets of user permissions, or you can select the permissions you want to grant. The Store Owner or a System Admin can create or delete users and grant permissions from Settings › Users.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: Permissions: Manage Settings
statement: Manage Settings Access Product Filtering, Store Settings, Checkout, Inventory, Order Notifications, Returns, Gift Wrapping, Conversions, and Gift Certificate settings. Must be enabled to download the Cyberduck Connection File and manage currency-specific Automatic Promotions.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: High-Risk Permissions: Edit Channels
statement: Edit Channels Edit channel settings and additional storefronts in the Channel Manager. This permission and Store Design are required to access the Theme Marketplace and the Edit Theme Files action in Page Builder for multi-storefront stores.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: Requirements: high-risk permissions
statement: Only the store owner user can grant high-risk permissions.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: User Roles: Store Owner
statement: Store Owner — Includes all permissions and is the person financially responsible for the account; this role has exclusive access to various account-related features.

identifier: Starting a BigCommerce Trial: Creating a Trial Store (the trial form)
statement: Fill out the form by providing your name, email address, a password, store name, the size of your business, and the region your store should be hosted. Note that the store name can be changed at any time after starting your trial.

identifier: Starting a BigCommerce Trial: Creating a Trial Store: hosting region
statement: Once you have selected a hosting region for your trial store, it cannot be changed. To ensure optimal site speed and performance, select the region nearest to your prospective customers.

identifier: Starting a BigCommerce Trial: Troubleshooting Failed Trial Creation: Common causes for trial failure
statement: Make sure that you are entering your actual business information in the form instead of placeholder data.

identifier: Starting a BigCommerce Trial: Troubleshooting Failed Trial Creation: Common errors: “An error had occurred while creating your trial. Please try again”
statement: There may be a mismatch with the country, date, or time settings between your browser and your store information. Check if one of the common causes could be the source of the issue and try again.

identifier: Account Dashboard: Updating Account Details (Account › Account details)
statement: To update your company name, VAT information, and manage contacts, click Account and select Account details from the drop-down menu.

identifier: Account Dashboard: Requirements (store owner)
statement: To access the Account Dashboard, you must be the store owner.

identifier: Account Dashboard: FAQ: What does the "We're having trouble updating your VAT Information. Please try again later" error message mean?
statement: This error can occur when there is an issue validating the VAT number with the issuing country. Contact our support team or create a Billing Case. Provide your VAT Number and Issuing Country in your case details.

identifier: Account Dashboard: Updating Your Payment Method (Account › Payment method)
statement: Click Edit to select and enter new payment details. The methods available to pay your invoice can vary depending on your store’s plan and region.

identifier: Account Dashboard: FAQ: Does BigCommerce send Form 1099-K for US taxes?
statement: No, Form 1099-K is issued by your payments provider(s).

identifier: About Your BigCommerce Invoice: Invoice Line Items: Related Transactions
statement: If the payment was not successful or your store is located in India, the payment must be made manually. For payment steps, see Paying an Invoice.

identifier: About Your BigCommerce Invoice: Paying an Invoice (India)
statement: Merchants in India must pay their invoice manually. If your business is located in India, you will be sent an email reminder on your billing date with a link to complete your payment.
scope: Merchants in India; a business located in India

identifier: About Your BigCommerce Invoice: Troubleshooting Payment Errors: Billing address mismatch
statement: If the billing address associated with your card does not match your BigCommerce account's address, the payment will fail. To update your account address, use the steps below. In the BigCommerce Account Dashboard, click Account and select Account details from the drop-down menu, then click Edit to the right of the contact listed as the billing contact.

identifier: About Your BigCommerce Invoice: Troubleshooting Payment Errors: MAX 7 error
statement: A “MAX 7” error occurs when the geographic distance between your billing address and the location you are attempting to make a payment from is too great. For example, attempting to pay an invoice while in a different country or using a VPN can result in a MAX 7 error. Our system uses your device's IP address to determine the zip code of your location when attempting to make a payment. To avoid this error, only attempt to process the payment while in the same zip code as your billing address.

identifier: Localization Settings: Physical Dimensions; Date and Timezone: Set standard formats for [country]
statement: To reset values to the standard formats for your store’s default country, click Set standard formats for [country].

identifier: Store Profile Settings: FAQ: Which countries support seamless translation in the storefront?
statement: If you create a new store based in one of the following countries, the store's content will be in your country's native language by default. All other countries and languages require theme lang file customization.

identifier: Date and Timezone Settings: Your Timezone (Settings › Date & Timezone)
statement: Your Timezone — the timezone where you are located. Determines times used when applying timestamps to orders and store logs.

identifier: Account Dashboard: Creating Additional Stores
statement: Multiple stores can be created under the same account, allowing you to manage them efficiently. These stores share the same contact and billing information.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (Settings › Store profile; Channels › Channel Manager › Storefront settings › Contact information)
statement: Go to Settings › Store profile to update or change your store's contact information. If you are using Multi-Storefront, go to Channels › Channel Manager, click on the name of your storefront, and navigate to Storefront settings › Contact information.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Address — The physical address of your store or place of business; appears on printed invoices and in the footer of most themes.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Address type — Specifies whether the above address is a home or commercial office, retail store, or warehouse.
